## R1. Noise protocol, seed-effect correction and strategies at budget 128 (2026-11-17, run 20261117T163106Z, commit 3ad3c9c)
**Setup.** `python benchmarks/harness.py --problems branin,hartmann6,mixed_hpo,sklearn_svm --noise-ratios
0.25,0.5,1.0 --arms random,lhs,tpe,gp,random-raw,tpe-raw --seeds 0-19 --budget 128 --jobs 4`: 1,840 runs, 0 errors,
964 s wall on the owner's Mac (4 processes). Problems and noise: `docs/plans/benchmarks.md` (noise SD = ratio × SD
of the true function over uniform points, half of its variance a per-seed offset shared by all candidates; the
scikit-learn SVM on digits has real split noise). 4 simulated workers, results arrive out of order. Arms: strategy
× protocol on (defaults, D8/D9/D14), off (`reeval_share: 0`, pick = best single observation) and raw (on, without
D14). Regret = optimum − true value of the pick (lower is better; the SVM uses the best true value seen in any run);
win rate = share of the 20 paired seeds where the first arm's pick has lower regret (ties ½). Tables:
`python benchmarks/overview.py benchmarks/results/sweep-2026-11-17/results.jsonl`.

**Interpretation.**
1. *Honesty of the reported winner (established here):* the D9 pick's reported value overstates its true value by
   about half as much as the best single observation (10 of 10 cells; e.g. mixed_hpo at noise 0.5: +0.033 vs
   +0.063 accuracy). This is the protocol's clearest effect.
2. *Quality of the pick (established here, small):* protocol on beats protocol off in mean paired win rate for every
   strategy (random 57 %, LHS 56 %, TPE 51 %, GP 64 %), and on the real-noise SVM task for all three strategies run
   there (random 78 %, LHS 65 %, TPE 60 %), at the cost of exploring about a third fewer candidates. It loses for
   random/LHS on Hartmann6 (42-48 %) and for TPE in four cells (Branin 0.5, Hartmann6 0.25 and 0.5, mixed_hpo
   0.25: 35-40 %).
3. *Selection, not search, is the bottleneck under noise (established here):* TPE's best-ever candidate is far
   better than its pick on Branin (regret 0.16-0.23 vs 2-8); with noise SD of a quarter of the function's spread
   or more, no rule could tell those candidates apart at this budget.
4. *D14 seed-effect correction (unresolved):* no measurable effect on the pick (mean win 50 % with TPE, 52 % with
   random; better in 6/10 cells with TPE and 4/10 with random, worse in 4/10 and 2/10). The smoke-run failure that motivated it does not recur at budget 128. Kept
   as the default because it is principled and costless here; real-noise data (simple_complex_v1) should decide.
5. *Strategies (established here):* TPE beats random in 7 of 10 cells (mean 64 %; 85-95 % on Hartmann6 and
   mixed_hpo at low noise) but loses on the SVM task (22 %) and low-noise Branin (25 %). LHS-only equals random
   (50 %). GP is the best arm on Hartmann6 at low noise (regret 0.05).

**Open problems.** The protocol's defaults (re-evaluation share 1/3, z 1.5, cap 6) were not tuned; TPE's losses with
the protocol (mostly at noise 0.25-0.5) suggest a lower re-evaluation share when the noise estimate is small (plausible, untested).
Synthetic noise is Gaussian with a fixed shared fraction; real training noise may differ.
